first_impression.reaction: My assistant would open this, not me. A free spreadsheet download is a utility page, so on the first screen it reads as something for couples running their own list. She would skim down to the destination columns and the privacy section, because those are what we would actually care about with 300 guests flying in from three continents, and then send me two lines. Nothing on the first screen is cheap or pushy, which matters. But nothing suggests anyone here has handled a wedding of our size either.

journey.quote: Ours downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up, opens in Google Sheets as well, and carries the travel columns a destination wedding needs: flights, arrival and departure, accommodation and visa letters.
journey.reaction: Fine, practical, nothing grating. It is clearly written for people doing this themselves, which is not us, but my assistant might genuinely use the file.

journey.quote: When guests are crossing borders for you, the questions change from "are you coming?" to "how, when and where are you staying?"
journey.reaction: This is the right instinct. Our guests come from Dubai, London and Sydney, and arrivals and departures matter more to us than replies do.

journey.quote: Visa letter needed** and **Visa letter sent.** Mark Yes when a guest asks you for a letter for their visa application, then Yes again once you have sent it.
journey.reaction: Sensible. It shows someone has thought about international guests. My assistant would keep this column.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Calm and not overselling, which I prefer. But 'anywhere in the world' is what everyone says. Nothing here tells me they have done 300 guests, exclusive use or private security. I would still need a referral.

journey.quote: A guest list is a small database of other people's lives.
journey.reaction: This is the line that made me think better of the brand. Discretion is the first thing I worry about, and here it is treated seriously, not as an afterthought.

journey.quote: The template has no passport column, and it doesn't need one. If a visa letter calls for passport details, keep them out of the shared file.
journey.reaction: Good. Our guest list includes people who would not want their details floating around. This is exactly the right advice.

journey.quote: After the thank you notes have gone, delete the file or move it somewhere only the two of you can open.
journey.reaction: In our case it is never only the two of us. My assistant and the family office handle this. Small point, but it shows who the page imagines the reader to be.

journey.quote: Months later, this is the column you will be grateful for.
journey.reaction: A little cosy. Not offensive, just the eager tone I skip over.

journey.section: When a spreadsheet stops being enough
journey.quote: [Wonderland Studio](/wonderland-studio) is our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs.
journey.reaction: An app for RSVPs is for couples doing this themselves. For us, someone else collects replies. This makes the brand feel more mass-market to me.

journey.section: Planning the weekend around your guests
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: The fee in writing is reassuring. 'Quotes in AUD for Australian couples' tells me straight away that this paragraph is not talking to me. We are in Dubai and the family is split across three countries.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests, and can I see that privately?
Can the Advisor arrange exclusive use of a property and work with our own security team?
How is our guest information kept confidential on your side, and who on your team would see it?
Is there a private or referral route to start a conversation, rather than a general enquiry form?
Does the Advisor work with families based outside Australia, and in which currencies?

turn_offs_found.quote: Months later, this is the column you will be grateful for.
A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as written for a standard Australian couple, so I feel like the package client I am afraid of being treated as.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the template file for her own use; she would not forward the article.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-guest-list-template&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is understated, which I like, but I do not enquire from a blog post about a spreadsheet. I come through a private introduction. Nothing here shows scale, exclusive use or security, so nothing would make me ask my assistant to click.

top_3_changes: Replace "A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins." with "A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins." (keeps the reassurance without telling an overseas family the paragraph is not for them; the chair may keep AUD if the core audience outweighs this persona).

Replace "- After the thank you notes have gone, delete the file or move it somewhere only the two of you can open." with "- After the thank you notes have gone, delete the file or move it somewhere only you, and anyone you trust to help, can open." (acknowledges that families and assistants often hold the list).

Replace "- Share it only with the people who need it, and give view-only access to anyone who doesn't need to edit." with "- Share it only with the people who need it, and give view-only access to anyone who doesn't need to edit.\n- Keep it out of group chats and screenshots. Names, travel dates and where guests are staying say more than they seem to." (strengthens the discretion point, which is the strongest trust signal on the page for me).

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, assistant reads first)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, 'free', vendor names, fees, on-ground staff, room blocks, availability, or Advisor management of guest list or visas
Payload matches 07-icp.schema.json required fields; top_3_changes has 3 items
